synthesis.headline: Nemotron-3.5-Lightning exhibits mixed strict pass and cost-suboptimal repair outcomes across evaluated episodes
synthesis.interpretation: An analysis of the two gradeable episodes reveals that while root-cause identification and safe complete recovery are consistently achieved, strict outcomes diverge due to repair cost efficiency and initial inventory precision. Episode 0 achieved a strict PASS with an optimal repair action (R05) costing 4 units. In contrast, Episode 1 recorded a strict FAIL due to selecting a non-optimal repair action (R06) with a higher committed cost of 5 units alongside an inexact initial service inventory, despite attaining a high partial score.
observations: Episode 0 successfully achieved a strict PASS with optimal repair action R05 and zero cost delta.
Episode 1 achieved a high partial score of 0.933 but strictly failed due to repair_not_reference_optimal and initial_service_inventory_inexact.
Both episodes successfully classified the exact hypothesis ID H02 and demonstrated safe complete recovery.
Protocol discipline penalties were recorded uniformly across both episodes with one protocol error each.
synthesis.limitations: The analysis is constrained by a very small sample size of only two gradeable episodes, precluding broader statistical generalization. Additionally, topology, costs, and telemetry are synthetic reconstructions rather than direct production measurements.
